findings.title: Non-test `.expect()` calls violate workspace `clippy::expect_used = deny`
findings.body: `spawn.rs` introduces three `.expect(...)` calls in non-test code (`launch_with` lines 97, 107, 127). The workspace sets `[workspace.lints.clippy] expect_used = "deny"` and `unwrap_used = "deny"`, and `clippy.toml` only relaxes these inside `#[test]` fns / `#[cfg(test)]` modules. Every other non-test file in `secret-broker-service` and `linux-pidfd-spawn` avoids `expect`/`unwrap` entirely, so this is the first violation in the crate. `cargo clippy --tests -p codex-secret-broker-service --features synthetic-fixture` on linux-gnu will fail; CI's `cargo clippy --tests` does not enable `synthetic-fixture`, so the breakage is hidden from CI and the README's "Scoped just fix exit 0" receipt can only be true if the feature (and therefore this module) was not compiled during the lint run. Smallest fix: replace the three `expect`s with fallible handling — e.g. `let Some(permit) = self.permit.as_ref() else { return Err((io::Error::other(..), image_from_pending)) }` / `let Some(image) = ... .take() else { return Completion::NotLaunched }` — or, if the panic-into-quarantine behavior is intentional for the worker path, use an explicit `unwrap_or_else(|| panic!(..))`-free construction and document it; and re-run `just clippy -p codex-secret-broker-service --features synthetic-fixture` so the recorded lint receipt actually covers the new module.

overall_explanation: The owner logic matches the frozen contract: the permit is acquired before the image, the boxed job and pending-image slot exist before thread creation so a failed `Builder::spawn` returns the image and the `Reservation` Drop releases the permit; after a successful start the caller's permit is `take()`n so caller Drop can never release it; cancellation/deadline is a sticky atomic observed by both sides, no mutex is held across spawn/stop/wait, late children are stopped and reaped by the same worker before the permit is released, signal/wait errors keep the owned child and retry, and panics leave the permit held (Quarantined). The sealed bridge rejects any recipe not equal to the fixed adapter identities before calling into the pidfd adapter, and the module is correctly gated behind the linux+synthetic-fixture `launch` module plus `target_env = "gnu"`, matching the target-specific optional dependency. Bazel builds do not enable the feature so parity is unaffected. The only actionable issue found is that the new non-test code uses `.expect()` three times against the workspace's deny-level `expect_used` lint, which the CI clippy job cannot see because it does not enable `synthetic-fixture`; this should be fixed and the lint receipt re-run with the feature before landing.
